architecture.title: Your first claw — from one install line to a local model
architecture.caption: You paste the installer line into the ⌨ terminal on the Spark; the runner never runs it for you. nemoclaw.sh installs Node.js, OpenShell and the NemoClaw CLI, then `nemoclaw onboard` (or Express Install) creates the gateway, the provider and the sandbox `my-assistant`. Inside the sandbox the harness calls https://inference.local; the gateway forwards it to local vLLM (:8000) or Ollama (:11434) on the same Spark. A direct call to api.openai.com has no network_policies entry and is denied. (Research tutorial Part 1, citing the DGX Spark NemoClaw playbook, the NemoClaw quickstart and the OpenShell playbook.)

sequence.title: L1.5 — three pieces of evidence that inference is local
sequence.caption: Evidence 1 comes from the host (`openshell inference get` names a local provider). Evidence 2 comes from inside the sandbox (`openshell sandbox exec -n my-assistant -- curl -s https://inference.local/v1/models` lists a model). Evidence 3 is a call that must fail (`curl https://api.openai.com/v1/models` from inside — Part 1, exercise 3); the denial shows in `openshell term` and `openshell logs my-assistant --source sandbox`. 1 + 2 are the Reef runner's pass criterion.
